findings: Non-blocking (binding gap): REVIEW_FILES in orchestrator/actions_runner.py omits scout.py (run_agent, the execution primitive the hosted adapter monkeypatches), orchestrator/campaign_lifecycle.py (require_review, used in the CI interpret gate), and orchestrator/publication.py (inventory, used by grounding). Post-review drift in these files will not trip REVIEW_BINDING_CHANGED. Mitigated: they can only change via separately audited/operator-driven publication routes, and the hosted control path itself cannot push commits. Recommend adding them to REVIEW_FILES or documenting the scoping.

Non-blocking (robustness, fail-closed): human_controls.save() enforces DANGER and size limits but not the control-character rule that validate_export/public_export.text enforce; a model answer containing e.g. \r or ESC produces a job failure with no artifact instead of a BLOCKED export. Consider applying public_export.text at save time.

Non-blocking (robustness, fail-closed): success evidence exceeding the 500KB bound (grounding context is duplicated across up to four prompt_* records) or an answer over 100KB converts an APPROVE-reviewed proposal into BLOCKED (EVIDENCE_PUBLICATION_REJECTED / PUBLICATION_TOO_LARGE) after full model spend. Consider excluding prompt records from public evidence or summarizing them by hash.

Non-blocking (documented recovery semantics): restore() replays any prior validated export for a request_id, including BLOCKED results from transient credential failures, permanently until the operator chooses a new request_id; receipt status is not distinguished on replay. Matches the workflow input documentation.

Non-blocking (documented residual): git_publication.scan applies the case-identifier (sub-stroke) refusal only to .json/.jsonl/.txt, consistent with the documented allowance for frozen cohort constants in reviewed .py/.md source; not new exposure, but arbitrary clinical prose in prose files is outside the regex boundary as the coverage doc already states.

Non-blocking (acknowledged trust limitation): reviewed() trusts repo-committed .execution.json/.response.json records; anyone with commit/publication access can fabricate a matching pair. Consistent with the stated position that this is an author-operated cross-family check, not independent desk approval; no new authority should be inferred from it.

Verified: fail-closed behavior on all traced failure paths (REVIEW_REQUIRED, CI identity, grounding, transport classification, export validation with no artifact-name release on failure); source==HEAD and branch-ref pinning; replay bound to identity hash, head SHA, workflow_dispatch event, and the control's workflow path with hash re-verification and content re-scan; traversal-safe structured outputs; scientific-approval preservation (PROPOSAL_ONLY interpret decision, REVIEWED_PROPOSAL_NOT_ADOPTED, no writes outside the pipeline directory, human_ratification:false, patient_execution:false, opposing-family receipts enforced, reviewer output cannot be prepopulated); privacy (private_evidence path stripped from projections, console/log files excluded from exports, tokens stripped from transport env, Authorization dropped on cross-host redirect, DANGER/size/control-character validation on all published text, env-var-mediated workflow inputs); dispatch limiter inactive by default with fail-closed ratified-path semantics and midnight-latched 2N halt. Source-only review; no tests were executed and no runtime behavior was exercised.
